acknowledged.reason: A timing side channel in RSA and in CBC/ECB decryption under LLVM's select-optimize, fixed in no release. The vendored subset has no RSA and decrypts only with GCM, CTR and CCM; the boards build with GCC.
A non-constant-time secret comparison in Prosody before 0.11.9; NVD names Lua 5.2 and later only as the runtime Prosody runs under. Nothing in Lua itself is affected, and the console runs no Prosody.

The unchecked offset is reached only through wasm_runtime_module_malloc and its kin, which no code of ours calls and whose callers in WAMR, libc-builtin and libc-wasi, are built out (WASM_ENABLE_LIBC_BUILTIN=0 and WASM_ENABLE_LIBC_WASI=0 on the boards, -DWAMR_BUILD_LIBC_BUILTIN=0 and -DWAMR_BUILD_LIBC_WASI=0 on the host).

fd_readdir is libc-wasi's, which no build compiles (WASM_ENABLE_LIBC_WASI=0, no libc-wasi in the vendored copy); a command's WASI is native/moy_wasm/moy_wasi.c, whose fd_readdir refuses a descriptor that is not a folder.
The strtol and strtoul wrappers are libc-builtin's, which no build compiles (WASM_ENABLE_LIBC_BUILTIN=0, no libc-builtin in the vendored copy).

fd_renumber is libc-wasi's, which no build compiles (WASM_ENABLE_LIBC_WASI=0, no libc-wasi in the vendored copy); native/moy_wasm/moy_wasi.c's fd_renumber answers fd_renumber(fd, fd) before it touches either descriptor.

Extended constant expressions are built out of the runtime (WASM_ENABLE_EXTENDED_CONST_EXPR=0 on the boards, WAMR's default of 0 on the host), where the advisory's module fails to load cleanly; wamrc compiles with them on, where a malformed module crashes only that compile.

wasi_thread_start is lib-wasi-threads', which no build compiles (WASM_ENABLE_LIB_WASI_THREADS=0 and WASM_ENABLE_THREAD_MGR=0, no lib-wasi-threads in the vendored copy); every export the console calls by name has its type checked first.
The wraparound is in the bounds checks wamrc emits for memory64, and the runtime is built without memory64 (WASM_ENABLE_MEMORY64=0), so its interpreter and AOT loaders both refuse a memory64 module.

wasi_sock_send is libc-wasi's and its race needs wasi-threads, neither of which any build compiles (WASM_ENABLE_LIBC_WASI=0, WASM_ENABLE_SHARED_MEMORY=0); native/moy_wasm/moy_wasi.c's sock_send reads no iovec and answers ENOTSOCK.
realloc is libc-builtin's, which no build compiles (WASM_ENABLE_LIBC_BUILTIN=0, no libc-builtin in the vendored copy).
